title: Kioku
description: A local-first .NET 10 MCP server that turns AI-agent project knowledge into durable Markdown records in an Obsidian vault, with typed contracts, engineering specs and plans, hybrid retrieval, coordination and multi-agent handoff workflows.
imageAlt: Kioku MCP server architecture and multi-agent handoff preview

caseStudy.problem: AI coding agents lose context when a session or process ends: decisions, specs, plans, bugs and project knowledge can stay trapped inside one conversation instead of becoming durable, reusable records. Kioku addresses that continuity problem by making project knowledge recoverable across fresh sessions and independent MCP clients.
caseStudy.approach: Kioku is a local-first Model Context Protocol server that reads and writes structured project knowledge directly in an Obsidian vault as Markdown and YAML frontmatter. The .NET 10 server exposes typed MCP contracts for specs, plans, decisions, bugs, sessions, queries, indexing and coordination, supports local stdio and authenticated Streamable HTTP, and keeps optional semantic retrieval and generation local through Ollama by default. Obsidian remains an optional UI integration rather than a runtime dependency for core workflows.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: The vault remains the human-readable source of truth instead of moving project memory into a hosted database. That keeps local ownership and offline inspectability, but it makes filesystem boundaries, concurrent mutation safety and explicit remote-transport security part of the product contract. Kioku therefore defaults to local stdio, restricts vault access, and requires authentication or explicit unsafe opt-in for non-loopback HTTP exposure.
caseStudy.outcome: Kioku 3.1.2 is the latest tagged server release and ships as the kioku-mcp-server NuGet tool. The v3 release line includes typed result contracts, coordination primitives, CAS-backed vault mutations, event history and a reproducible multi-agent handoff demo; 3.1 adds first-class engineering specs and durable SPEC → PLAN workflow support. The public repository also documents generated MCP contracts, deployment, security and retrieval behavior.
learnings: Durable, human-readable Markdown survives session and process boundaries better than provider-specific conversation history.
Generated contracts and explicit SPEC → PLAN → SESSION boundaries make agent workflows easier to recover across clients and fresh sessions.
Remote MCP access needs explicit authentication, origin and filesystem boundaries instead of inheriting the trust assumptions of a local stdio process.

problem.label: PROBLEM
problem.title: SESSION CONTEXT IS NOT DURABLE
problem.body: AI coding agents lose context when a session or process ends. Decisions, specs, plans, bugs and project knowledge can remain trapped in one conversation instead of becoming reusable project records.

approach.label: APPROACH
approach.title: LOCAL-FIRST MCP + OBSIDIAN
approach.body: Kioku reads and writes project knowledge as Markdown and YAML frontmatter in an Obsidian vault. Typed MCP contracts expose specs, plans, sessions, queries and coordination over local stdio or authenticated Streamable HTTP.

tradeoffs.label: TRADE-OFFS
tradeoffs.title: LOCAL-FIRST BY DEFAULT
tradeoffs.body: The vault stays the readable source of truth and core workflows work without Obsidian open. Remote HTTP is supported, but non-loopback exposure requires explicit authentication and security configuration.

outcome.label: OUTCOME
outcome.title: PUBLISHED V3 WORKFLOW AND HANDOFF CONTRACT

Keep retrieval or performance metrics tied to their documented environment, dataset and methodology instead of presenting them as universal SLAs.

architecture.caption: Current public model: MCP clients connect over local stdio or authenticated Streamable HTTP to the .NET 10 Kioku server, which exposes typed tools, prompts and resources over a strict vault boundary. Core workflows read and write the Obsidian vault directly; semantic retrieval, Ollama and the Obsidian bridge remain optional integrations.

security: The Obsidian vault is the local source of truth; writes remain inside the configured vault and external reads or permanent deletion require explicit opt-in.
Streamable HTTP binds to loopback by default; non-loopback exposure requires an API key unless an explicit unsafe override is configured.
Optional Ollama embeddings and generation keep note content local under the default configuration, while the Obsidian bridge uses separate authentication.
testing: The public repository contains automated server tests and release/build workflows alongside generated MCP-contract checks.
The repository documents installation and execution through both local stdio and Streamable HTTP deployment paths.
This portfolio does not claim an independently rerun release-wide test count; current implementation evidence remains inspectable in the Kioku repository.
deployment: The server ships as the kioku-mcp-server NuGet global tool for local installation and stdio use.
Authenticated Streamable HTTP supports long-running deployments, with loopback-safe defaults and explicit configuration for broader exposure.
The optional Obsidian plugin is maintained in sandovaldavid/kioku-obsidian with independent versioning, keeping server and UI-bridge release concerns separate.
limitations: The develop branch can move beyond 3.1.2, so branch-specific generated contracts are required before presenting develop behavior as released.
No release-wide test suite was independently rerun for this portfolio review; repository tests and workflows are inspectable evidence rather than a reproduced validation result here.
Local-first deployment means operators remain responsible for vault access, authentication and network exposure when enabling remote HTTP.
No external adoption, production workload or commercial impact is claimed for this project.
